allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Because of the actions of her irresponsible parents, a young girl is left alone on a decrepit country estate and survives inside her fantastic imagination.

facts.overview: Because of the actions of her irresponsible parents, a young girl is left alone on a decrepit country estate and survives inside her fantastic imagination.
facts.title: Tideland

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Left entirely on her own in a crumbling house, where do the borders of her protective fantasies end and real-world peril begin?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Abandoned on a decaying country estate due to the reckless actions of her parents, a young girl retreats into a vivid, surreal inner world to endure her profound isolation.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Slow, somber, and deeply imaginative, balancing emotional heaviness with tense, engaged isolation best suited for solo viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Terry Gilliam, this singular drama blends dark fantasy and suspense to craft a heavy, unconventional portrait of a child's psychological resilience.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: Two items sit near the tolerance line. 'Abandoned' can imply deliberate desertion, where the overview says only that she is 'left alone' 'because of the actions' of her parents, and those actions could have many forms. I read it as ordinary shorthand for being left alone, since the copy pairs it with the same cause the packet gives. 'Real-world peril' in curiosityHook implies that external danger exists and that fantasy and reality blur. The overview does not state either, but the Thriller genre and the suspenseful mood support tension, and the phrase names no concrete threat. A stricter adjudicator could ask for it to be softened toward the source's own 'survives inside her fantastic imagination', which would make it a MINOR causal or mechanistic concretization.
